question: Are Cottonwood Heights storm and informational routes competing for the four fixed commercial queries, or does the selected main page have a broad-intent alignment gap?

decision.summary: The August 12 fixed mobile panel selects the self-canonical Cottonwood Heights city page for all four commercial queries at positions 15, 10, 15, and 14. The exact Search Console request returns no rows for those four queries, which is unknown or withheld demand rather than zero. The storm child and wind guide have strong aggregate visibility for storm-specific demand, but no measured fixed-query association. The main page has 21 inbound internal links and its title and H1 emphasize premium reroofing while the fixed panel targets broader roofing-contractor, repair, replacement, and roofer intent. Preserve every route and consider only a later owner-gated title test.
limits: A targeted Search Console request with no returned row means unknown or withheld demand, not zero impressions and not proof that no URL is indexed.
Search Console is blended across devices and its window ends three days before the fixed mobile panel.
Aggregate storm-route visibility is separate from fixed commercial query-to-page attribution and must not be treated as cannibalization proof.
The fixed panel is one mobile Android location sample per query and must be repeated weekly before a keep/revert decision.
Service-area inclusion for Cottonwood Heights on the current Salt Lake Valley profile remains unverified, so this diagnosis does not authorize GBP, Maps, hasMap, or sameAs changes.

hypotheses.why: The current panel consistently selects the intended city page, but the page remains outside the top ten for three queries. Its title and H1 use the narrower premium-reroofing framing, while roofer and roofing contractor are absent from visible main-page copy.

The current mobile panel selects the main page for all four commercial queries. Search Console returns no exact fixed-query rows, so strong aggregate storm demand cannot identify the storm child or wind guide as a commercial-query competitor.

The guide uses exact roof-replacement language but has only six aggregate impressions and four inbound links. No fixed-query row attributes roof replacement cottonwood heights to it; preserve and monitor.

The exact Salt Lake Valley CID does not appear in any of the four Cottonwood Heights local packs, and current profile service-area inclusion has not been verified. This can affect Maps but does not authorize a profile mutation.
